title: Pseudo-coherence in a distinguished triangle
statement: Let R be a ring and m an integer. Call an object C of D(R) m-pseudo-coherent if there are a bounded complex E^\bullet of finite free R-modules and a morphism E^\bullet\to C in D(R) inducing isomorphisms H^i(E^\bullet)\to H^i(C) for i>m and a surjection H^m(E^\bullet)\to H^m(C). In a distinguished triangle K \to L \to M \to K[1] in D(R) [def-pc-derived-category], if K is (m+1)-pseudo-coherent and L is m-pseudo-coherent, then M is m-pseudo-coherent.
